note: Proposed defaults, chosen from what each target and the test hardware need, before any v1 score existed. Not tuned on the test places.

land_rule.plain: A cell counts as land when at least 5% of it is land.

scoring.yearround_reason: A quarter of the year-round score: enough that a place usable only a few months drops clearly, not so much that season alone outranks the match.

slope: Slope limits rovers and landers before anything else does.
safe10: NASA's lander limit is 10°, so the share of ground under it decides where a lander can touch down.
relief: Height range matters for long drives and line of sight, less than the local slope.
highland_rock: Rock family matters for digging and building, but the rock map is coarse and only knows "plutonic".
bare: Rovers and builders work on open ground; at the pole there is nothing else.

frozen: Ice-cemented ground is the base's main water source, the first resource to practise on.
highland_rock: Oxygen comes from the highland rock; the rock map only finds its family.

dry: The only trait in this challenge.

cold: Deep cold drains batteries and stiffens seals.
season_swing: The yearly swing cycles every joint and seal; as important as the cold itself.

sun_height: The only trait in this challenge.

flat5: Pads, roads and solar farms need ground under 5°.
low_relief: Long straight strips, like a railgun, also need little height change.

slope: Slope limits rovers and landers before anything else does.
safe10: Lander safety is judged on the share of ground under 10°.
relief: Height range matters for long drives, less than the local slope.
minerals: Mineral-bearing ground is what Mars rovers drive to; EMIT covers only dry land, so it gets one share.
bare: Mars ground is all bare; plants change how wheels grip and dust lifts.

frozen: Water: frozen ground is where teams practise drilling for buried ice. Used when the target has a frozen-months value; otherwise Resources is minerals alone.
minerals: Water-bearing clays and sulfates are the other water source on Mars.

dry: The only trait in this challenge.

cold: Cold nights drain batteries and stiffen seals.
day_swing_ground: The daily swing cycles every joint and seal every sol; ground is matched to ground.
day_swing_air: Used when the target has an air value instead; air is matched to air.

dust: Dust in the air is what coats solar panels and clogs filters.
bare: Dust is lifted from bare ground; plants hold it down.

minerals: Water-made minerals are where traces of past life are kept. One share, not more, because EMIT sees only dry land, so most places have no mineral data.
dry: Dryness preserves traces and slows decay.
bare: Bare ground lets instruments reach the rock.

surface: On the Moon only Surface can be scored for driving; Moon dust is a label.
Slope and footing decide where a rover can drive.
atmosphere: Dust and haze wear down wheels, joints and solar power, but slope comes first.

resources: Water and oxygen from the ground.
heat: Heating and cooling are the main load on life support.
light: Power at the pole comes from a low sun.

terrain.order_reason: A cell gets at most one type: the first rule it meets, in this order. The narrowest rules go first, so a salt flat inside a dry basin is called a salt flat.

validation.pass_marks_note: All pass marks were set on 15 November 2026, before any v1 run. Moon part 2 uses 0.8, the same mark as every other analog-against-ordinary comparison, instead of the plan's example of beating every ordinary place.
